p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** The concrete grammar for a package reference, the table of legal forms and where each is legal, worked examples with invented groups, the rule for what persisted state stores, and the shape a collision error must take.

grammar.title: The grammar

p.a-reference-has-up-to-four-parts: A **reference** (the thing a manifest lists or a human types) has up to four parts:

grammar.fence:
ref := [ kind ":" ] [ group "/" ] name [ "@" version ]
group := segment ( "." segment )* segment := ( lower | digit | "_" | "-" )+ name := ( lower | digit | "_" | "-" )+ kind := ident ; type tag: "flow", "plugin", "lib", … version := <a version requirement in your scheme, e.g. semver>
lower := "a" … "z" digit := "0" … "9"

p.THREE-AXES-THREE-SEPARATORS: **Three axes, three separators.** The type tag, the group, and the version each attach with a *different* delimiter — `:` then `/` then `@` — so the parser never has to guess which axis a token belongs to.

p.THE-DELIMITER-CHARACTERS-ARE-A-DESIGN-CH: The specific delimiter characters are a design choice; the load-bearing rule is that the three axes stay lexically distinct.

p.PICK-THREE-THAT-DO-NOT-COLLIDE-AND-NEVER: Pick three that do not collide with your version syntax and never overload one.

td.ROW-FORM-BARE-NAME-WHERE-LEGAL: CLI input only — resolved once via the index

td.ROW-FORM-KIND-AND-NAME-WHERE-LEGAL: CLI input only — kind is validated after resolution

td.ROW-FORM-VERSIONED-WHERE-LEGAL: anywhere a specific release is meant

facts.RULE-MANIFESTS-ACCEPT-QUALIFIED-FORMS-ON: **Manifests and lockfiles accept the qualified forms only.** A bare or kind-only name is never written to persisted state (see [§storage](#storage)).
facts.RULE-THE-CLI-ACCEPTS-ALL-FORMS: **The CLI accepts all forms.** It is the one place a human is present, so it is the one place a short name may be resolved.

p.DOCUMENTED-EXAMPLES-ARE-COPIED-AND-RUN: Documentation examples are not illustrations — readers copy them and run them. So the form an example shows is a claim that the command works when pasted, and that claim differs by verb.

td.ROW-DOC-INSTALL-WHY: works unconditionally; a short name needs a configured registry index, which the reader may not have

td.ROW-DOC-UNINSTALL-UPDATE-WHY: resolves from the lockfile alone — no network, no index — and it is what a person actually types

td.ROW-DOC-FILE-CONTENTS-WHY: the only form ever stored there, per [§storage](#storage)

p.THE-ASYMMETRY-IS-THE-POINT: **The asymmetry is the point, and it is not tidiness.** A short name in an install example fails for a reader whose registry index is unconfigured, while a qualified name in an uninstall example is merely longer than what anyone would type. The rule follows the failure, not the symmetry.

p.SHORT-FORMS-IN-DOCS-ARE-NOT-ERRORS: **A short form in documentation is not an error to be swept.** It is legal input and it is implemented; this policy governs what NEW examples should show, and existing ones are corrected where a reader would actually be misled — not counted and mass-replaced. A worked example naming a package that does not exist has no qualified form to be rewritten into.

p.THE-KIND-TAG-VALIDATES-IT-NEVER-DISAMBIG: **The kind tag validates, it never disambiguates.**

p.THE-RESOLVER-CHECKS-THE-TYPE-AND-ERRORS-: If a reference carries `kind:`, the resolver checks that the resolved package's type matches, and errors on a mismatch.

p.A-REAL-AMBIGUITY-IS-ALWAYS-A-GROUP-COLLI: It cannot pick between two packages, because `(group, name)` is already unique — a real ambiguity is always a *group* collision, resolved by qualifying the group, never by adding a kind.

examples.title: Worked examples

p.invented-groups-lead: Invented groups, to keep the mechanics product-neutral:

examples.fence:
cart # bare — CLI sugar; resolves if exactly # one group owns a package named "cart"
com.example.shop/cart # qualified — the form a manifest stores
plugin:com.example.shop/cart # fully explicit; "plugin" is checked # against the manifest after resolution
com.example.shop/cart@1.4.0 # a specific release
io.acme/logger@^2.1 # a version *requirement*, not a pin; # the lockfile records the pin it chose

p.manifest-fragment-lead: A manifest fragment, after the tool resolved a human's `add cart`:

p.THE-HUMAN-TYPED-THE-SHORT-NAMES-THE-TOOL: Note what is *not* here: no bare `cart`, no `logger` — the human typed those, the tool stored the qualified forms.

p.the-single-storage-rule-stated-once: The single storage rule, stated here as the anchor every restatement echoes:

quote.PERSISTED-STATE-IS-QUALIFIED-ONLY: **Persisted state is qualified-only.** Every reference written to a manifest, a lockfile, or a dependency edge carries its group. Short names exist solely as human CLI input and are rewritten to the qualified form the instant they are resolved.

facts.CONSEQUENCE-A-LOCKFILE-ENTRY-CARRIES-THE: A **lockfile** entry carries the full tuple: `group`, `name`, the resolved `version`, and the `content-hash` that pins the bytes. Two registries serving the same hash under the same `(group, name, version)` are the same locked entry — the registry is a fetch detail, not part of the lock's identity.
facts.CONSEQUENCE-THE-GRAPH-IS-BUILT-FROM-QUAL: The **dependency graph** is built entirely from qualified names, so a short name never recurses into it. This is the mechanism behind the protocol's "no transitive collisions" guarantee — it is enforced *by the storage rule*, not by a separate check.
facts.CONSEQUENCE-A-PUBLISHED-PACKAGES-REQUIRE: A **published package's own `[requires]`** is qualified, because its author published through the same boundary. You never inherit another author's short name.

errors.title: Error shapes

p.A-MACHINE-FACING-FAILURE-MUST-BE-ACTIONA: A machine-facing failure is only useful if a script or an agent can act on it without reading prose.

p.a-collision-must: **A collision** (one short name, several owners) must:

facts.COLLISION-EXIT-WITH-THE-COLLISION-CODE: exit with the collision code — distinct from the conflict code, so a caller branches on the number alone;
facts.COLLISION-LIST-EVERY-CANDIDATE: list **every** candidate, each with its exact qualified form; and
facts.COLLISION-TELL-THE-HUMAN-WHAT-TO-TYPE-NE: tell the human precisely what to type or record next.

errors.fence: "cart" is ambiguous — 2 packages match: 1. com.example.shop/cart (registry shop-public) 2. io.acme/cart (registry acme-internal) Re-run with the qualified form, e.g. install com.example.shop/cart

p.THE-CANDIDATE-LIST-IS-THE-WHOLE-POINT: The candidate list is the whole point: the human copies one line and records it.

p.THERE-IS-NO-INTERACTIVE-MENU: There is **no interactive menu** — a picked choice leaves no record of *why* that group; a pasted qualified name is self-explaining.

p.A-CONFLICT-IS-A-DIFFERENT-FAILURE-WITH-A: **A conflict** (unsatisfiable versions) is a *different* failure with a *different* code.

p.a-conflict-names-the-incompatible-constr: It names the incompatible constraints and the packages that imposed them, so the human can relax one:

errors.fence: version conflict on io.acme/logger: com.example.shop/cart requires ^2.1 org.example.tools/audit requires <2.0 no version satisfies both.

p.a-caller-that-cannot-tell-them-apart-wil: A caller that cannot tell these two apart will retry a collision as if it were a conflict, or vice versa.

p.DISTINCT-STABLE-CODES-KEEP-AUTOMATION-CO: Distinct, stable codes are what keep automation correct.

facts.SUM-A-REFERENCE-IS-KIND-GROUP-NAME-VERSI: A reference is `[kind:][group/]name[@version]` — three axes, three distinct separators; the delimiter characters are a choice, the distinctness is the law.
facts.SUM-BARE-AND-KIND-ONLY-FORMS-ARE-CLI-SUG: Bare and kind-only forms are CLI-input sugar; qualified forms are legal everywhere.
facts.SUM-THE-KIND-TAG-VALIDATES-THE-RESOLVED-: The kind tag validates the resolved type; it never disambiguates.
facts.SUM-PERSISTED-STATE-IS-QUALIFIED-ONLY: Persisted state is **qualified-only** — that storage rule is what makes transitive collisions impossible.
facts.SUM-A-COLLISION-LISTS-CANDIDATES-A-CONFL: A collision lists every candidate with copy-ready qualified forms and fails; a conflict is a separate failure with a separate, stable machine code.
